chapters.title: When EF becomes a DTO factory
Long-term value of doing EF right

takeaways: Scaffolding tables into hollow DTO-style entities scatters business logic across services and makes EF feel bloated.
Micro-ORMs suit narrow read-heavy endpoints, but in complex domains you end up rebuilding change tracking, relationships and concurrency that EF already provides.
Put behavior into entities and use navigation properties, owned types and the fluent API to keep persistence details out of the domain model.
hook: Many .NET teams use Entity Framework as a table-to-class generator, then blame EF when their code turns into scattered services and duplicated rules. This episode shows developers how to spot the DTO factory pattern, when a micro-ORM really makes sense and how to model real domain logic with EF Core. The payoff is simpler tests, less duplication and clearer code.
